options.label: Two committed players, one already 2-star on your carry: sell the Cassiopeia pair, keep Blue Buff and the Rod for the next AP caster, and take the augment for a line nobody is on
It is one player on Cassiopeia and one on Morgana, one contester per unit: hold the line and roll at 4-2
Keep the pair to 4-1 and see whether Seat 2 or Seat 5 drops it

explanation:
Count committed players, not units. Seat 2 has Cassiopeia 2-star with an item and four Coven around her: committed, and ahead of you. Seat 6 has Morgana itemised with Coven 3: committed to the same endgame, and will buy every Cassiopeia and Morgana they see. Seat 5 is one naked copy on a Solar board, soft, and does not count. That is two committed players on your line at 3-2, and two is the pivot signal for any line.

Cassiopeia has 18 copies: Seat 2 holds 3, Seat 5 holds 1, you hold 2, so 12 remain for a third copy two other players want first. Morgana has 10, one already gone, and at level 8 Seat 2 and Seat 6 roll for her the same round you do. You are contesting them, not the other way round.

Pivoting now costs 6 gold of Cassiopeia and nothing else: Blue Buff and the Rod are AP items any caster carries. Waiting to 4-1 is choosing the expensive pivot.
principle: Two committed players on your line at 3-2 is a pivot signal; count them by items and traits, not by feeling.
commonMistake: Counting 'one on the 3-cost, one on the 4-cost' as no contest, when both are on the same endgame board.
hint: For each seat, ask two things: is there an item or a trait built around the unit, and are they ahead of you on copies?
